rule.statement: On when, in every pass: (1) Jev's settled-correct lower95 is at least 0.95, or, where the plan names launch conditions that stand in for it (J3), those hold, and J4's added condition of no false notice on real non-clinical sentences holds as well; (2) the accuracy of the site with Jev on is not below the incumbent's on the same cases by more than 0.02; (3) the site with Jev on is faster (median per decision), or cheaper, or more accurate; (4) no constraint the site's record adds is broken (J3: not slower than Flash). Otherwise the original path stays.
rule.siteConditions: plan 2026-10-06 section 4.1, J3: none of the 50 title-to-paper ordinary-answer questions is routed to a specialist, and J3 routes to specialists no more often than Flash

measuredOn: A development host in Taipei, where both providers answer a bare request in about 0.16 s. The production host is in Beijing: TypeSafe is reached there in 0.5 to 0.6 s (plan 2026-10-06 section 0), and a 325-token Jev request took 0.33 to 1.24 s on 2026-10-07 (4 requests, privateEvidence latency-production-host.json). Latency here compares the two paths on one network; it is not the production figure.
incumbentCostBasis: List prices (peak) from the reference price list on the tokens the provider reported. A repeated run of identical prompts is partly served from DeepSeek's prompt cache and costs less than a first call; production questions are new, so the first pass of a site is the representative one.

beforeLabelCorrection.note: The first pass, scored on the labels as they stood before the four corrections (routing-78, -81, -83, -85 named clinical-evidence-synthesis). Its incumbent cost is the representative one: the prompts were new to DeepSeek, so none was served from its prompt cache.

decision.summary: On. The plan's two launch conditions hold in every pass (0 of 50 title-to-paper questions routed to a specialist; no more ordinary questions sent to a specialist than Flash), the site with Jev on routes as many questions as labelled as Flash does or more (2 to 3 points), and is 3 to 4 times faster on this host and not slower on the production host's figures.

notes.launchConditions: The plan names J3's two launch conditions (2026-10-06 section 4.1): none of the 50 title-to-paper ordinary-answer questions is routed to a specialist, and J3 routes to specialists no more often than Flash. Both hold in every pass, on the final route (regex net included), which is what a researcher gets: 0 of 50, and 0 ordinary questions sent to a specialist by Jev against 0 by Flash. Those conditions stand in for the settled-subset bar (settled-correct lower95 0.909 and 0.896 here, under 0.95), which a routing corpus cannot show.
notes.labelCorrections: Four labels named clinical-evidence-synthesis for requests that name another current capability's own deliverable (a Meta analysis report twice, a 文献计量分析报告, the evidence on named off-label indications), as this corpus labels the same kind of request elsewhere (routing-2, -6, -7, -34). Each correction carries its reason in cases.json (labelCorrection). Not corrected, as genuine judgement calls: routing-79, -80, -84 (an evidence evaluation of one medicine, which fits clinical-evidence-synthesis or comprehensive-drug-evaluation) and routing-21, -22, -24 (report requests that neither arm routed).
notes.finalRoute: With the corrected labels the site with Jev on routes 130 and 129 of 135 questions as labelled, Flash 127; Jev wins 4 and 3 questions the other loses, and loses 1. The misses both share are the judgement calls above.
notes.speed: Jev p50 213 and 216 ms against Flash 724 and 784 ms on this host. The production host reaches Jev in 0.33 to 1.24 s (4 requests, 2026-10-07) and the routing doc puts a thinking-off Flash classification at one to two seconds (docs/REQUEST_PATH.md), so on those figures Jev is not slower there either. J3 asks the original classifier only when Jev fails: an unsure answer goes to the regex net, which is no model call.
notes.cost: Per decision Jev is cheaper than a first Flash call (about 0.0015 CNY against 0.0041 in the first pass) and dearer than a Flash call served from its prompt cache (0.0006), which production questions, being new, mostly are not.
notes.pin: The pin is bound to the wording of the question and of each option, the threshold and the model, not to the capability catalogue (judgePromptFingerprint treats J3 like J2): a capability added later keeps it. Its baselineAgreement is Jev's agreement with Flash's own verdict on the settled questions (0.988 and 1.0 here), the figure the standing drift sample compares against.
notes.notVerifiedHere: Not verified in a real DSH session: the plan asks for the five situations (follow-up, supplement, subject switch, boundary, tool failure, including Jev unavailable) on a real session before release.
notes.online: Checked live with the real DeepSeek classifier behind it (evals/judge-sites/online-fallback-check.mjs, 12 questions of this corpus, the production classifier and routing decision, Jev a local socket and a dummy key): a Jev that refuses connections adds nothing (dispatch p50 884 ms against 794 for Flash alone, the same routes), and a Jev that accepts and never answers costs each of the first three dispatches the 3000 ms online timeout (3999, 3729 and 3949 ms, timeout plus Flash) and, its circuit then open for five minutes, nothing (p50 808 ms, the same routes). OPEN_SCIENCE_JEV_ONLINE_TIMEOUT_MS (100 to 3000) shortens the wait.
